submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole detects that the text it is reading is repeating itself: activation at a token grows with how much of the current token, its word, and the sentence frame around it has already occurred earlier in the same context (it rises with the number of previous occurrences and with the number of consecutive tokens of the matching span already re-read), and it is near zero on first mentions in prose that keeps introducing new material. The strongest activations (2.5-2.9) occur only inside long self-similar stretches - keyword-stuffed pharmacy keyword lists, thesaurus row templates, repeated maths/proof templates, refrain-like prose - and the unit is retrospective: its write direction suppresses the most frequent tokens (the, comma, and) instead of promoting a specific next token.
